page_title: mcpock — checks every MCP server your AI agents use

summary.name: mcpock
summary.one_liner: A small macOS menu bar app that checks the MCP servers your AI agents use and flags the ones that are broken, slow, waiting for sign-in, or set up differently.
use_cases: find which MCP server an AI agent cannot use
diagnose broken or slow MCP servers
check MCP servers waiting for sign-in
verify MCP setup across multiple AI agents
let an agent check MCP servers before starting
summary.what_it_does: The app reads MCP server configs for many AI agents (including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot) and checks each server the way the agent would. It reports which servers are broken, slow, waiting for sign-in, or configured differently. Each problem comes with a reason and a suggested fix, written for both the user and their agent. Saving a config triggers a recheck of that server within seconds. The app only reads configs and does not change them. It also ships its own MCP server so an agent can check before it starts.
notable: Checks MCP servers the way each agent would, across 20+ AI agents
Includes its own MCP server so agents can check before starting
Reads configs locally; no account, no analytics
Fix status updates automatically after a config is saved
caveats: Mac-only: the page names macOS as the platform
Page does not describe any paid tier; listed as free with no subscription
